e201.text: Last time, we found three animal groups. Amphibians, birds and fish. Three more to go!

e202.text: An ant and a spider. Which one is the insect?

e301.text: It's You against the Buddies. You lock in first. One finger for every point. A little animal is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

e401.text: Round one. Which one is an insect? One, the ant. Two, the spider. Show me with your fingers.

e403.text: Two. It is tiny, and it crawls. Like a bug!

e405.text: One! But how do we know?

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

e601.text: Count with me! One, two, three, four, five, six. Six legs!

e602.text: Two feelers on its head. And three body parts.

e603.text: Now the spider. Eight legs! No feelers. Two body parts.

e604.text: The ant is the insect! The spider is not. It belongs to a different group.

e608.text: Insects have six legs and a pair of feelers. The body of insects is divided into the head, thorax and abdomen.

e609.text: Insects have an outer covering that is usually hard and shell-like.

e701.text: Many adult insects have two pairs of wings. Some adult insects have only one pair of wings. Some do not have wings at all.

e801.text: My rule! If it has wings, it is an insect. A butterfly. A pigeon. Both insects!

e802.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

e803.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! A pigeon has feathers. It is a bird. Count the legs, not the wings!

e901.text: Round two. A monitor lizard! Its skin is dry and scaly. Which group? One, amphibians. Two, reptiles. Three, mammals. Show me with your fingers.

e903.text: One! Four legs, like a frog.

e904.text: Two. Its skin is dry, not moist.

e1003.text: I knew it! I'm a reptile!

e1004.text: Most reptiles, except snakes, have four legs.

e1005.text: Reptiles usually have dry and scaly skin. They breathe through their lungs.

e1006.text: Most reptiles reproduce by laying eggs.

e1101.text: Be a scale! Shrink down. Quietly.

e1102.text: You are one scale on a monitor lizard's back. You are dry, and tough.

e1103.text: Early morning. The air is cool, so you are cool. The lizard is slow.

e1104.text: Now it crawls into the sun. Sunlight lands on you. You warm up!

e1105.text: At noon, it is too hot. Splash! Into the cool lake. You cool down.

e1202.text: Reptiles are cold-blooded animals. This means that they do not have a constant body temperature like humans. Their body temperature changes with the environment that they are in.

e1203.text: Cold-blooded does not mean I am always cold. I warm up in the sun!

e1301.text: Show me your score hand! More than two? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

e1302.text: Did you spot the hidden animal? It was the grasshopper, on the lamp post! Is it an insect? Tell someone at home.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

e1401.text: Next: this animal has wings. It flies at night. Is it a bird? Find out in Part Two!
